caption: Figure 6: Permutation invariant MNIST 784-1000-1000-10 model negative log likelihood and test error with layer normalization and batch normalization. (Left) The models are trained with batchsize of 128. (Right) The models are trained with batch-size of 4.
description:
This figure presents two sets of plots comparing the performance of different normalization techniques in neural networks. Each set contains two graphs: one for negative log likelihood (NLL) and one for test error. The left set of plots shows results for models trained with a batch size of 128, while the right set shows results for models trained with a batch size of 4. The series are labeled as BatchNorm bz128, Baseline bz128, and LayerNorm bz128 for the left set, and LayerNorm bz4, Baseline bz4, and BatchNorm bz4 for the right set. The LayerNorm bz128 series shows the lowest NLL and test error in the left set, while the BatchNorm bz4 series shows the lowest NLL and test error in the right set.

Description: at most 120 words. What kind of conclusions can be drawn from the figure.

The figure suggests that Layer Normalization (LayerNorm) is more effective than Batch Normalization (BatchNorm) in stabilizing training, especially with smaller batch sizes. The LayerNorm bz128 model shows the lowest negative log likelihood and test error in the left set of plots, indicating better performance with a larger batch size. Conversely, the BatchNorm bz4 model shows the lowest NLL and test error in the right set, suggesting that BatchNorm performs better with a smaller batch size. This indicates that LayerNorm may be more suitable for larger batch sizes, while BatchNorm may be more effective for smaller batch sizes.
